episodes.215547: As a storm system and cold front moved through Middle Tennessee on August 22, 2026, scattered thunderstorms developed, especially across the Cumberland Plateau. Abundant instability and forcing from the front caused these thunderstorms to become severe. Several reports of downed trees and large hail of 1 to 1.5 inches were received.
episodes.215573: A couple clusters of thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front that approached late in the evening.
episodes.215579: Bands of thunderstorms ahead of an approaching cold front produced localized wind damage and a few instances of large hail from eastern West Virginia into the north-central Virginia Piedmont.
episodes.215608: A storm system moved into the area from the northern Rockies, generating some strong thunderstorms, some of which became severe as they moved from central Montana through northeast Montana.
episodes.215778: Storms along and behind a warm frontal passage began to form in an environment with ample instability, moisture, and shear during the evening hours of August 22, 2026. These storms initially began to exhibit upscale growth across western Pennsylvania, producing large hail in Elk County as that specific storm moved north-northeastward into McKean County and produced an isolated instance of tree damage. Further south, a line of thunderstorms spanning across Clearfield and Cambria Counties shifted further eastward with embedded circulations beginning to form. One of these circulations produced an EF-1 tornado in Madera before lifting and producing straight-line wind damage closer to Clearfield-Centre County line. This storm continued to produce isolated wind damage further eastward into Centre County. Across southern Pennsylvania, slow-moving severe thunderstorms produced multiple instances of flash flooding in Somerset and Bedford County with isolated wind damage across Bedford, Fulton, and Franklin Counties.
episodes.215807: Three rounds of thunderstorm activity occurred from late on August 20 through the evening of August 22. One decaying MCS crossed into northeastern Central Alabama early on August 21, causing scattered tree damage across Cherokee, Etowah, and St. Clair counties. Scattered activity occurred during the evening of the 21st, including in Barbour, Marengo, and Tallapoosa counties. The third round came on the evening of the 22nd, with another MCS moving down the I-22 corridor through Marion, Fayette, and Walker counties, weakening below severe limits before reaching the Birmingham metro area.
episodes.215903: Thunderstorms developed in a very unstable atmosphere. The first round of thunderstorms produced one to three inches of rain, with the second round producing another one to three inches. This resulted in isolated flash flooding with the second round of rainfall. Localized rainfall amounts of two to six inches were observed.
episodes.216217: Both low pressure and a cold front tracked through the region and produced flash flooding.
episodes.216228: A cold front stalled across Eastern North Carolina during the afternoon hours of August twenty-third. This combined with ample instability and wind shear over the Carolinas resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms developing along and out ahead of this front across the Coastal Plain. This activity then tracked east with a few of these storms becoming severe in nature bringing strong wind gusts to portions of the inland rivers, Pamlico Sound, Core Sound, and coastal waters north of Cape Hatteras during the afternoon and evening of August twenty-third.
episodes.216249: August proved to be a very active weather month as daily chances of showers and storms stretched into the 22nd and 23rd. The culprit behind this timeframe of storms came in the form of a warm front shifting just north of the area on the 22nd and a cold front approaching from the west. This front arrived during the evening, then progressed east across the area overnight. ||Showers and storms accompanying these fronts produced one to two inches of rain across ports of southeast Ohio. Heavier rainfall amounts upstream led to flooding on West Fork Duck Creek at Macksburg. Damaging winds also accompanying these storms resulted in a cluster of tree and power line damage noted across much of southeast Ohio before the front's departure to the south late on August 23rd. In the town of Wellston, multiple downed trees fell down into nearby homes. The risk for thunderstorms quickly came to an end once the frontal boundary completed its passage through southeast Ohio.
episodes.216250: Active weather continued to stretch into the second half of August across West Virginia under the guise of a warm front and cold front combination sweeping through the region. A swath of tree and power line damage was noted across north-central West Virginia on the afternoon of August 22nd while warm and unstable conditions thrived ahead of the frontal passage. The front completed its journey through the area by late in the day, bringing the severe threat to an end.
episodes.216365: During the afternoon of August 22, a thunderstorm developed over southeast Weld county along an outflow boundary. This storm quickly intensified as it moved northeast and approached I-76 near the Weld/Morgan county line, where it produced a significant swath of damage from Empire Reservoir through Jackson Lake State Park. A storm survey was conducted on August 25, which revealed a swath of significant straight line wind and wind-driven hail damage along a 11 mile path. Maximum wind speeds were estimated at 80 mph, along with a maximum hail size of approximately 2 inches in diameter.||In addition to this storm, a severe thunderstorm dropped 1.5 inch diameter hail and produce wind gusts up to 67 mph across western Arapahoe County. A third severe thunderstorms also brought hail up to 1.25 inch in diameter to the Brighton and Fort Lupton area.
episodes.216477: Several isolated to scattered severe thunderstorms moved across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska, producing large hail and strong wind gusts. Heavy rain also occurred.
episodes.216478: Any isolated severe storm moved across the northern Nebraska Panhandle and produced very strong wind gusts. Severe Thunderstorm Watch 618.
episodes.216592: An approaching cold front over the Ohio Valley produced isolated severe thunderstorms across the northwest Piedmont during the late evening hours. Damaging wind reports were observed across Forsyth County.
episodes.217476: A small cluster of storms lead to some wind damage in Georgetown County, SC.
episodes.217559: Heavy downpours from afternoon thunderstorms caused some street flooding.
episodes.217641: A long-lived thunderstorm produced strong to severe wind gusts across portions of far southern Oklahoma to near Wichita Falls, TX on the late evening of the 22nd.
episodes.217683: An MCS began to track southeast from eastern Kansas during the morning of August 22nd. Model soundings across the Mid-South depicted an inverted-V with mid-level lapse rates around 7.0 C/km. By the afternoon hours, a large bow began to race across the Mid-South with a large swath of damaging winds in its path.
episodes.217729: A broad sub-tropical ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over Texas and the southern Plains resulting in a deep layer northerly flow regime in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a weak mid-level trough axis was oriented in a west to east fashion along the I-10 corridor, and a weak stationary front was positioned along the I-20 corridor.  An isolated severe thunderstorm producing damaging wind gusts developed along the mid-level boundary  on the I-10 corridor in Tangipahoa Parish in the afternoon hours and then swept southward  in Lake Pontchartrain before dissipating in metro New Orleans.
episodes.217730: A broad sub-tropical ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over Texas and the southern Plains resulting in a deep layer northerly flow regime in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a weak mid-level trough axis was oriented in a west to east fashion along the I-10 corridor, and a weak stationary front was positioned along the I-20 corridor.  An isolated severe thunderstorm producing strong wind gusts developed along the mid-level boundary on the I-10 corridor in Tangipahoa Parish in the afternoon hours and then swept southward across Lake Pontchartrain before dissipating in metro New Orleans.
episodes.217858: A shortwave trough moved across the northern rockies, causing the high pressure to shift back westward. Deep monsoonal moisture in place and the forcing from this shortwave trough resulted in thunderstorm development with heavy rainfall causing flash flooding and debris flows mainly impacting the burn scar areas, particularly the Gold Mountain Burn Scar and Lee Burn Scar. Storms training over the Lee Burn Scar in particular resulted in debris flows and mudslides both on the 23rd and 24th of August.
episodes.217883: High amplitude upper level ridging began shifting east of the region late on the 21st into the 22nd. This allowed for a deep southerly flow aloft to advect in monsoonal moisture, which resulted in two days of strong to severe thunderstorms across the region. Forecast soundings for the 22nd were not overly supportive of widespread strong wind gusts (Modestly deep inverted-V profile), with only one observation reaching severe criteria. A cold front approaching the area on the 23rd maximized warm air advection and allowed for numerous thunderstorms to develop in the warm sector. The main concern with the setup was for sub-optimal kinematics - thermodynamics and forcing were both more than sufficient. Quite a few severe gusts were observed on the 23rd, making it the much more active day compared to the 22nd.
episodes.218125: Shortwave energy and a weak front approaching the region along with deep moisture residing across the local area favored thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds and heavy rainfall.
episodes.218126: Shortwave energy and a weak front approaching the region along with deep moisture residing across the local area favored thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds.
episodes.218188: A line of showers and thunderstorms moved through western and central North Dakota during the afternoon and evening along a surface trough, with a few scattered severe reports coming from Billings, Ward, and Dunn Counties. The largest hail of 1.5 inches in diameter was reported in Billings County west of Medora, and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated up to 70 mph in Dunn County east of Mandaree.
episodes.218206: Following the cold front on the 22nd, a trailing surface trough axis crossed Lake Erie during the evening hours of the 23rd. The warm waters of Lake Erie helped a modest amount of instability develop over the lake, with relatively strong winds in place aloft. This allowed thunderstorms that swept across the lake along the trough to produce strong, gusty winds, particularly in the waters offshore of the Cleveland area.
episodes.218267: Strong to severe thunderstorms brought all modes of severe weather, including a reported tornado.
episodes.218296: A warm and moist airmass was in place across the region on August 22. Isolated to scattered slow-moving storms resulted in flash flooding near Norfolk and across the VA Eastern Shore.
episodes.218299: A warm and moist airmass was in place across the region on August 22. Isolated to scattered slow-moving storms resulted in gusty winds on the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.218417: A cold front pushing through the region helped spart a cluster of thunderstorms that moved through southwestern VA. One storm briefly became severe, producing isolated wind damage.
episodes.218455: Multiple severe weather reports were received along with minor debris flow near the Heise burn scar.
episodes.218478: The subtropical ridge established itself once again with weak troughing off the Pacific Northwestern U.S. coastline. With robust moisture return in place, this would set the stage for flash flooding across southern Utah and scattered instances of severe thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts across northern Utah.
episodes.218597: A cluster of thunderstorms developed from lee convergence convective lines extending northeast offshore the Lower Florida Keys.  A waterspout was observed north of Big Pine Key.
